newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bus hijackers in Russia demand ransom - official.
newsitem.headline: Bus hijackers in Russia demand ransom - official.

text.p: Two or three "bandits" hijacked a bus with 35 people aboard in the southern Russian region of Dagestan on Monday and are demanding $100,000 ransom, a spokesman for the Interior Ministry in Moscow said.
He could not confirm a news agency report that the hijackers were Chechens. Dagestan borders breakaway Chechnya. The spokesman said he had no other details.
The spokesman said the hijackers had demanded a helicopter. He could not say where they wanted to go.

RIA news agency earlier quoted Dagestan interior ministry chief-of-staff Sultan Gantilov saying there were two hijackers and that they were Chechens. He said they seized the bus in the Dagestan capital, Makhachkala, and were heading for the airport.

Last January Chechen separatist guerrillas led by Salman Raduyev took hundreds of hostages in the Dagestan town of Kizlyar and then withstood days of Russian bombardment in the village of Pervomaiskoye before escaping back across the Chechen border.
Monday's incident was more reminiscent of hijackings by Chechens before war broke out in Chechnya in December 1994. Small groups held up buses for ransom in neighbouring regions on several occasions.
